title: The model lineup was pruned and replanted
summary:
The model lineup changed, the community directory grew, and the examples and referral links got a little more deliberate.

Text API work spanned routing, aliases, and the advertised catalog. DeepSeek-V3 routing was tidied up; `openai-large` moved to GPT-4.1 on April 15, then its underlying model changed again alongside `openai` on April 19. After a catalog cleanup, configuration added `openai-reasoning` with text and image input, `llama-vision` for image understanding, and `gemini` using Gemini 2.5 Flash Preview. The model list was less of a fixed menu than a garden this week.

The directory gained wearable and web image tools, Indonesian-language generators, a vector-making tool, a web simulator, Discord and chat bots, and a project focused on African languages and cultural contexts. MCPollinations joined the SDK and Libraries list as a way for AI assistants to use the image, text, and audio APIs; its author credit was corrected the next day. These are community-built projects and listings, not new Pollinations features.

Affiliate translation now checks the full content before deciding its language, helping avoid unnecessary translation of English text. Referral matching gained affiliates and no longer requires Markdown-formatted responses; the chance of a fallback Ko-fi link and the overall frequency of referral links were reduced.

The website’s Python image example now creates a `pollinations.Image` with the chosen settings before calling `Generate`. The OpenAI-compatible text-to-speech POST example now shows both text and audio modalities and puts `voice` and `format` inside the `audio` object.
